newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran, Iraq to swap bodies of soldiers killed in war.
newsitem.headline: Iran, Iraq to swap bodies of soldiers killed in war.

text.p: Iran and Iraq will on Tuesday exchange the remains of 75 soldiers killed during their 1980-88 war, the official Iranian news agency IRNA said on Sunday.
It quoted Brigadier General Mifaisal Baqerzadeh, head of Iran's committee for the missing in action, as saying the bodies of 20 Iranians would be exchanged for those of 55 Iraqi soldiers.
Baqerzadeh said the planned swap follows talks between Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati and his Iraqi counterpart to improve relations.
"Military experts from both sides are to conduct technical studies on joint research operations," IRNA quoted Baqerzadeh as saying, without elaborating.

Both sides have swapped prisoners of war and remains of soldiers. But the missing in action and the POWs are still among the thorniest issues hindering efforts to improve ties between the former foes.
Iran has said 5,000 to 10,000 prisoners are held by Iraq. Baghdad denies holding any Iranians and says more than 20,000 Iraqis are held by Tehran.
